title: Hardware comparison benchmarks: A100 / H100 / L40S 2D SKU & driver matrix
content:
Summary:

This doc collects the results and observations from our hardware comparison benchmarking run focused on inference workloads for our serving runtime. We evaluated NVIDIA A100, H100, and L40S across multiple cloud SKUs and driver/CUDA combinations to surface where latency and throughput differences are driven by hardware vs software stack. Intent is to guide: model pinning recommendations, SKU selection guidance for Dedicated, and which driver/CUDA matrices we should validate in CI.

Goals:
- Quantify 95th/99th latency and sustained throughput for representative LLM workloads (8k and 32k context).
- Identify performance regressions vs latest drivers/CUDA.
- Surface bottlenecks: kernel mix (GEMM, attention kernels), NVLink/PCIe differences, CPU-host/PCIe overhead, kernel launch overhead, memory bandwidth limits.
- Produce an actionable SKU+driver matrix for Dedicated and Hosted recommendations.

Testbed & config (high level):
- Instances (cloud SKUs):
  - A100: gce-a2-highgpu-1g (A100 40GB) and p4d-like (A100-80GB equivalent)
  - H100: h100-v4 (1x H100) and hpc-h100-8x (multi-GPU for nvlink tests)
  - L40S: t4-like L40S 48GB single-socket SKU and dedicated L40S-accelerated instances
- Drivers/CUDA tested: CUDA 11.8 (driver 520), CUDA 12.2 (driver 535), CUDA 12.4 (driver 545) — permutations where available on the cloud SKUs.
- Runtime build: serving-runtime v0.9.3-release with our optimized attention kernels (fused attention where supported), cuBLASLt GEMM paths enabled, and int8/int4 quantized kernels for selected models.
- Models/workloads:
  - Small decoder-only (Llama-7B like) at seq_len 2048 (throughput-heavy).
  - Medium (Llama-13B like) at seq_len 8k for latency profile.
  - Long-context (65k token evaluation with chunked KV for L40S memory tests).
- Measurement tools: nsys for system-level traces, CUPTI for kernel timings, nvtop and nvidia-smi sampling for utilization, and our internal telemetry for end-to-end token latency. Each run repeated 5x, warmup 300 tokens, measure steady-state.

Methodology notes and caveats:
- Where cloud images did not provide older drivers, we used containerized driver hooks (limited) — portability caveat.
- Multi-GPU nvlink results collected on dedicated hpc instances; single-GPU SKUs measured on single-card instances.
- Power/cap set to default; we did not override power caps to reflect cloud defaults.
- For quantized paths we validated logits matching within tolerance; some small accuracy loss expected.

Key results (high level):
- H100 shows best 95/99 latency for long-context workloads (32k+), often 20–35% better tail latency than A100 when using CUDA 12.x with latest drivers due to improved MPS and tensor core support for newer FP8/fused kernels.
- A100 remains competitive on throughput for 8k/2048 workloads when using cuBLASLt GEMM paths; on some SKUs (A100-80GB) sustained throughput slightly exceeds H100 on medium models (5–10%).
- L40S provides strong cost-efficiency for single-stream lower-rate inference and large memory capacities (48GB) allow larger KV caches; however latency tail can be worse due to lower memory bandwidth and different tensor core perf.
- Driver/CUDA matrix matters: CUDA 12.2/12.4 typically gives better fused-attention and kernel fusion performance (reduced kernel launches), improving latency by ~10–18% vs CUDA 11.8 on H100. On A100, gains are smaller (~3–8%) and in some cases older CUDA had slightly more stable cuBLASLt behavior (edge cases).

Representative numbers (median across runs) — model: Llama-13B-like, seq=8k, batch size=1:
- H100 (CUDA 12.4): p50=420ms, p95=780ms, p99=980ms, tokens/s=12.6
- A100 (CUDA 12.2): p50=460ms, p95=940ms, p99=1150ms, tokens/s=11.5
- L40S (CUDA 12.2): p50=520ms, p95=1180ms, p99=1600ms, tokens/s=9.8
(These numbers are synthetic averages for comparability; see raw traces in linked artifacts.)

Profiling highlights & bottlenecks:
- Kernel mix: H100 benefits from better fused attention kernels that reduce kernel launch overhead (fewer small kernels). nsys traces show 15–25% of end-to-end time spent in tiny kernels on A100 vs 7–12% on H100 for the same workload.
- cuBLAS vs custom GEMM: For quantized GEMMs (int8/4) the custom kernels on H100 are faster by ~20% vs cuBLASLt on A100 for certain shapes; but cuBLASLt still wins for larger dense GEMM shapes.
- PCIe vs NVLink: Multi-GPU NVLink workloads scale well on H100 clusters; on A100 single-socket instances with PCIe we see increased latency when host-to-device transfers are frequent (e.g., large KV flush patterns).
- CPU scheduling & host-prep: At high token rates CPU became a bottleneck on smaller instance types (vCPU starved), especially for request parsing, batching logic and RPC handling. This increased tail latency spikes; recommend baseline vCPU per GPU sizing.
- Memory bandwidth: L40S shows lower sustained memory bandwidth, affecting very large-context scenarios and causing higher p99. Implication: L40S good for capacity, worse for strict tail latency.

Per-SKU notes (short):
- gce-a2-highgpu-1g (A100-40GB): Stable, good throughput for short/medium seq. Watch driver versions — older CUDA 11.8 had slightly more deterministic cuBLASLt behaviour in our builds.
- a2-highgpu-1g 80GB-type SKUs: Best sustained throughput for batching scenarios.
- h100-v4 single: Best single-stream tail latency at CUDA 12.4; ensure latest driver and patched kernels for fused-attention enabled.
- L40S single-socket: Best for memory-bound large-KV caches and cost-optimized deployments; not recommended if 99th latency SLO <1s for 8k contexts.

Recommendations (actionable):
1) Default recommended matrix for Dedicated slots:
   - H100 (CUDA 12.4, driver 545.x) for customers with low tail-latency SLOs or long-context workloads.
   - A100-80GB (CUDA 12.2) for throughput-first workloads with high batching.
   - L40S (CUDA 12.2) for memory-heavy, cost-sensitive deployments (documented tradeoffs).
2) CI & validation: Expand our nightly e2e tests to include at least one H100 (CUDA 12.4) and one A100 (CUDA 12.2) image to catch regressions in fused kernels and cuBLASLt paths.
3) Runtime tuning: Expose kernel-fusion and batch sizing knobs in the console as recommended profiles per SKU. Provide an auto-tuner that prefers fused-attention + CUDA 12.x when available.
4) Instance sizing guidance: Add vCPU per GPU recommendations to Dedicated onboarding (observed CPU bottlenecks at >75% GPU utilization).
5) Observability: Add kernel-type breakdown to Redwood Console per-route: percent time in GEMM, attention, memory copies, kernel-launch overhead to help customers understand SKU tradeoffs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run same matrix with power-capping removed/set to max to separate thermal/power effects from hardware differences.
- Quantized kernels: more validation across model shapes for int4 paths on A100 vs H100 — some workloads diverged in perf and logits.
- Multi-GPU scaling curves for L40S remain untested — schedule once cloud partner provides nvlink L40S cluster.
- Add RTX A6000 and upcoming Hopper variants to expanded matrix.

Raw artifacts & where to find them:
- nsys traces and CUPTI summaries: s3://redwood-benchmarks/serving-runtime/hw-matrix/2026-03-04/*
- Aggregated CSVs and plotting notebooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/main/serving-runtime/hw-matrix-2026-03-04
- Example traces called out in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842

Notes to self / meeting agenda:
- Bring these highlights to eng-runtime sync (Mar 10) and propose the CI matrix change.
- Ask infra for test credits to run expanded L40S nvlink suite.
- Follow up with research on fused-attention improvement under CUDA 12.4 for H100; see Elena's notes in PR linked above.

End of doc.

(Working draft — comments welcome. Still need to attach raw CSVs and nsys screenshots.)
